_header: Diego Venegas-Vargas | DAMIC-M collaboration | CCDarkSens Framework -- Example scan config: WIMP-nucleon spin-independent limit reproduction of DAMIC 2016 (0.6 kg-day, PhysRevD.94.082006) with the joint 1x1 + 1x100 likelihood in the cluster-energy analysis space; companion of wimp_nucleon_damic2016_limit_repro.json (1x1 only).
_comment: WIMP-nucleon SI exclusion-limit reproduction, DAMIC 0.6 kg-day (PhysRevD.94.082006 / arXiv:1607.07410), Fig. 11 -- JOINT 1x1+1x100 likelihood version, companion to wimp_nucleon_damic2016_limit_repro.json (1x1-only). Same halo/grid/rates_dir as the 1x1-only config; only response.cluster_fit_mc is replaced by response.channels[]. 1x1 channel: same paper-fit params as the single-channel config (11x11 window, sigma_pix=1.8e-, background 15x365.25=5478.75 events/(kg yr keV)). 1x100 channel: one_dimensional=true (window_ny=1 -- the paper's row-summed 1D readout, PhysRevD.94.082006 Sec. VI, NOT a literal 2D fit on a 1-row window), background 21x365.25=7670.25 events/(kg yr keV) (paper Sec. VIII, line 539). sigma_pix_e=1.8 for 1x100 is carried over from the paper's general detector characterization -- not separately restated for 1x100 in the paper text, flagged as an assumption (see configs/wimp_nucleon_cluster_damic2016_1x100_repro.json's own _comment for the full paper-citation trail). Each channel's own NLL is minimized independently at fixed sigma (the background nuisance parameters don't couple between channels) and summed before the UL crossing search -- see docs/ClusterFitMC_Design.md for the derivation of why this is exact, not an approximation, for background_model=scale. Pipeline: 1) python3 utils/wimp_nucleon_generate_grid.py configs/wimp_nucleon_generate_si_damic2016halo.json (shared rate CSVs, same as the 1x1-only config -- no need to regenerate) 2) ./build/ccdarksens_scan_generic configs/wimp_nucleon_damic2016_limit_repro_joint.json 3) ./build/ccdarksens_plot_limit outputs/wimp_nucleon_damic2016_limit_repro_joint/scan_generic.root "CCDarkSens joint repro" --wimp --batch --x-min 400 --x-max 12000 --y-min 1e-41 --y-max 1e-35 --out-pdf <path>.pdf FURTHER UPDATED: rates_dir now uses quenching.model=chavarria_izraelevitch_table (adds Izraelevitch et al. 2017, arXiv:1702.00873, real measured quenching data 2.28-20.67 keV_nr) instead of chavarria_table (which fell back to unconstrained Lindhard theory above 2.28 keV_nr) -- see python/ccdarkphys/wimp_nucleon/quenching.py. FURTHER UPDATED: background_efficiency_csv per channel (Fig. 9 digitized curve) + folding-bug-fixed (Sec. 6.8).
